topic: Henyey-Greenstein (1 - g^2) energy-conserving cloud phase function vs unnormalized forward lobe blowout rig
topic_zh: Henyey-Greenstein (1−g²) 能量守恒云雾相函数对比未归一化前向波瓣银边过曝爆炸
scope: Deterministic Henyey & Greenstein (1941) energy-conserving phase normalization ((1 - g^2) / (1 + g^2 - 2g*mu)^(3/2)) versus naive unnormalized forward-scattering lobes and 64-subinterval spherical quadrature across 17 anisotropy stations (g in [0.05, 0.85]). No neural cloud relighting execution.

protocol.function: ½ ∫_{−1}^{1} (1 − g²) / (1 + g² − 2gμ)^{3/2} dμ ≡ 1.0000 → 100% Energy Conserved Across All g

robustness.name: Sampled 17 scattering anisotropy stations lock spherical integral at 1.0000 without energy creation

good_fit: Single and multiple scattering in volumetric clouds, god-rays, and underwater media (Horizon Nubis, UE5 Volumetric Cloud, Flight Simulator)
Proving why the (1 - g^2) numerator is mandatory to cancel the 1/(1 - g^2) integral growth of the (1 + g^2 - 2g*mu)^(-3/2) forward lobe
Blending dual-lobe Henyey-Greenstein (forward g_1 = +0.80 silver-lining + backward g_2 = -0.30 glory) while preserving unit total energy
Replacing 64-subinterval spherical phase integration with closed-form O(1) normalized lobe evaluation
not_for: Pure Rayleigh molecular sky scattering where the symmetric 3/4*(1 + cos^2 θ) phase function applies
Opaque surface BRDFs without participating media or subsurface volumetric scattering
Neural cloud relighting or 2D skybox style-transfer networks
Non-scattering pure absorption filters (scattering albedo ω_0 = 0)
